affectedPublicSurfaces: THE CELERY BEAT SCHEDULE — the operational surface this slice actually changes, and the only public surface it changes. `workers/celery_app.py::beat_schedule` holds SIX entries today, VERIFIED 2026-09-08: `mock-analytics-hourly-reconcile` (:44, `crontab(minute=0)`), `cdp-batch-staggered-reconcile` (:51, BARE `crontab()` — EVERY MINUTE), `analytics-backfill-topup` (:59, `crontab(hour=2, minute=17)`), `daily-impact-reader` (:81, `crontab(hour=3, minute=23)`), `reap-abandoned-workflow-runs` (:97, `*/5`) and `credential-refresh-beat` (:110, `*/30`). A seventh entry appears here. THE ISSUE BODY'S PHRASE 'the four at `:00`' IS WRONG ABOUT THE CODE: exactly ONE entry is at `crontab(minute=0)`, and `cdp-batch-staggered-reconcile` is a bare `crontab()` that fires every minute of every hour — so a literal reading of 'no two entries share a minute-and-hour' is UNSATISFIABLE against that entry, and the collision rule must be stated as Meta means it: the new entry shares no minute-and-hour with any FIXED-TIME entry (`minute=0`, 02:17, 03:23) and does not land on a `*/5` or `*/30` boundary. Decide it deliberately and say so in the PR. The 02:17 and 03:23 minutes are not decoration — they carry #1659's lesson in their own comments. A beat entry is a standing commitment on a shared worker fleet: its cadence, its per-shop fan-out and its behaviour on a missed tick are the release risk, not the code.

NO HTTP SURFACE CHANGES. There is no route, no response model and no seller-visible string in this slice. `POST /v1/action-cards/refresh` — whose task `services/action_cards/refresh.py` is `run_fujiwa_poll_cycle`'s ONLY live caller today — keeps its path, its cooldown gate and its response byte-identical. Nothing a client can call behaves differently.

`inventory_items` STOPS BEING EMPTY. That is a data-shape change every downstream reader feels even though no reader's code moves. ADR-087:89 and the scope verification both record the table at zero rows; `forecaster.py:181` reads `InventoryItem` and gets nothing today, and five readers have been running against an empty table. After this slice they see rows. A reader that silently depended on the empty result — a `max()` over an empty sequence, a divide guarded only by emptiness — will start executing a path it has never executed in production. Enumerate the five readers and state in the PR what each does with a non-empty result.

ONE ADDITIVE, NULLABLE `committed_quantity` COLUMN on the inventory row, and the transform that fills it. The vendor returns `total_committed_quantity` plus a per-warehouse `committed_quantity` (contract-collection A-8:304, `samples/inventory-search-response.json:23,27`), and every layer drops it today, VERIFIED 2026-09-08: `expand_inventory_search` (`integrations/tiktok/mapping.py:396-433`) emits only `sku_id / product_id / available_quantity / warehouse_id / seller_sku` — and at `:414-420` it takes the FIRST warehouse and `break`s, so a multi-warehouse SKU loses the rest before the committed number is even considered; `normalize_inventory` (`mapping.py:437-465`) synthesises only `available_quantity`/`quantity`; `_transform_inventory` (`services/etl/transform.py:230-253`) collapses to the single `"quantity"` at `:238-243`. `committed_quantity` is read NOWHERE in `backend/src` today and `models.py:265-289` has no such column. S-FR-6's "never below a committed quantity" and CE-3's Luôn sẵn hàng exclusion have no data at all without it. NOTE THE BOUNDARY: this slice persists the committed quantity for the identity the table already has — `ix_inventory_shop_sku` is `(shop_id, tiktok_sku_id)` (`models.py:282-287`), warehouse is NOT in the key — and does NOT change that identity. Per-warehouse identity `(shop, sku, warehouse)` and the first-warehouse-only fix are #1794/#1795 in a DIFFERENT epic's lane; keeping the first-warehouse behaviour here is deliberate and must be stated in the PR, not fixed in passing.

PER-TENANT SCOPE ON A SCHEDULED WRITER (S-NFR-8 / ADR-089). The task resolves its tenant and does every tenant read and write inside `with_shop_scope` (`database/tenant_context.py:346`). Enumerating the shops is the ONE sanctioned unscoped step. This is a fleet-wide behaviour, not a per-request one: a single unscoped query "for efficiency" writes one shop's vendor data into another shop's rows and no HTTP test would ever see it.

`inventory_items.velocity` IS NOT A SURFACE AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE. `_transform_inventory` writes the literal string `"low"` for every row (`transform.py:245`; `normalize_inventory` never emits a velocity) and nothing reads it — a consumer-without-producer inverted. Leave it exactly as it is or delete it in a stated, separate decision; do NOT let the excess signal grow a dependency on a constant.

migrationCompatibility.notes: ONE ADDITIVE, EXPAND-ONLY migration adding a NULLABLE `committed_quantity` column to the inventory row. Nothing is dropped, renamed or retyped; there is no NOT NULL and no backfill — an existing row simply carries NULL until the next cycle rewrites it, and NULL means 'not yet observed', never zero. Old and new code coexist: the previous release neither reads nor writes the column and keeps writing `quantity` exactly as before. THE MIGRATION NUMBER AND `down_revision` ARE RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update`, but W6, W8, W9 and the sibling W10 lanes all hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake. The table is tenant-scoped, so the new column must be covered by the runtime role's existing per-table grants from `043_juli_app_role.py` (ADR-085) and by the existing RLS policies — assert that coverage as `juli_app`, never as the owner. Do NOT alter `ix_inventory_shop_sku`: it is the idempotence guarantee the second acceptance criterion rests on, and widening or dropping it turns a re-run into a duplicate writer. Do NOT add a per-warehouse identity column here — `(shop, sku, warehouse)` identity is #1794's, in a different epic's lane, and starting it here forks the schema.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. `beat_schedule` keeps its six entries, `run_fujiwa_poll_cycle` keeps its single manual caller in `services/action_cards/refresh.py`, `inventory_items` stays empty, and `committed_quantity` stays dropped at all three layers. Every Clear Excess slice downstream stays blocked on the same missing rows they are blocked on today — the pre-existing state, unchanged, with nothing partially applied and no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: REMOVE THE BEAT ENTRY FIRST, then redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api, juli-celery-worker and juli-celery-beat. Order matters: a beat process still holding the new schedule keeps enqueueing a task the redeployed workers no longer define, producing a queue of permanently failing messages. With the entry gone, nothing is scheduled and the previous code runs correctly with the `committed_quantity` column present — it simply never names it and needs NO downgrade. Rows already written are ordinary inventory rows the manual refresh would have produced anyway, so no data is lost and no reader breaks. Only if the schema must ALSO be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1` drops the nullable column, which destroys the committed-quantity observations and nothing else; that downgrade must fail loudly with a named error rather than proceed silently if any consumer of the column has already shipped. State in the PR the one thing that does NOT roll back: the shop now has inventory rows, and every downstream reader that had only ever seen an empty table continues to see a non-empty one. No run can be in `waiting_external` on account of this slice, so no drain is required here.
